metadata.title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Ramp Metering Based on Traffic Video Data
supplementary_materials: "The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request."
"An initial draft of this paper was submitted as a preprint in the following link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.12104"
metadata.hardware_requirements: "computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)"

nodes_source.source_quote: The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.
nodes_source.description: Empirical traffic data from a freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao in Shandong, China, used to calibrate simulation parameters.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Data is stated to be available upon request from the corresponding author; no public URL or DOI is provided.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31]. The simulation is performed in the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao
nodes_process.description: A microscopic traffic simulation is set up based on empirical data from a real-world freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao. The network incorporates speed limits, and traffic is simulated from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, 1/1 tool explicitly named, 3/3 key configuration parameters stated; however, exact empirical traffic flow demand generation details are missing.

nodes_process.node_name: Video Frame Preprocessing and State Stacking
nodes_process.source_quote: After zooming and down-sampling, the size of one observation is 4 x 512 in pixels. Three consecutive observations are stacked to represent the traffic state.
nodes_process.description: Traffic video frames are extracted, zoomed, and down-sampled. Three consecutive 4x512 pixel frames are stacked to form a sequential state matrix input representing vehicle positions for the RL agent.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, basic matrix/image operations required with no specific tool named (which is acceptable), and all necessary dimensional parameters are given.

nodes_process.source_quote: A multitask learning strategy is implemented in the training process... While training the ramp metering Q-network, the mean speed in the merging area and the queue length... are predicted
nodes_process.description: A Deep Q-Network is trained over 10^6 frames using multi-task learning. The network uses three CNN layers and one FC layer to predict Q-value, mean speed, and queue length concurrently.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, optimizer named but core deep learning framework is omitted; excellent parameter coverage with nearly all hyperparameters strictly defined in Table 1.

nodes_process.source_quote: For comparative purposes, two scenarios are also considered in the evaluation. The first scenario does not apply ramp metering, and the second scenario adopts the PI-ALINEA method.
nodes_process.description: The baseline control strategies are instantiated: a no-control scenario and the PI-ALINEA method. Regulator parameters for PI-ALINEA are fine-tuned to minimize mean travel times.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, baseline mathematical formulation (Eq 13) and all critical parameters are fully explicitly stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments. The simulations for the training phase and each experiment are initialized with different random seeds.
nodes_process.description: The DRL method is evaluated against baseline scenarios across 20 simulation experiments initialized with random seeds. System metrics like travel times, mean speed, and queue length are extracted.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, test procedure and number of trials is explicit, but the specific set of random seeds is not disclosed.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data... The information in the subarea is removed from original data to generate perturbed data
nodes_process.description: An ablation study evaluates the algorithm's robustness by spatially dividing the camera control area into eight subareas and systematically removing input from each to measure impact on travel time.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, the perturbation logic is clearly defined and visualized (Fig 15), and the evaluation sample size and subarea count are fully specified.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The training process, presented in Figure 8, can be finished in less than 24 hours... The episode reward and mean travel time are both converged in 400,000 training frames
nodes_sink.description: Convergence curves for episode reward and mean travel time during the training phase.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Hyperparameters and SUMO simulator specified, but exact training scripts, environment wrappers, and raw empirical input data are not publicly provided.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Median and interquartile ranges of vehicle travel times in the mainline over time for No control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear statistical visualization of simulation outputs. Reproducibility is limited by the lack of open simulation code and exact traffic input profiles.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments. It is found that the performance of the PI-ALINEA method is not always better than that of the no-control scenario.
nodes_sink.description: Mean travel times across 20 distinct simulation experiments (random seeds) for No controls, PI-ALINEA, and DRL, including percentage changes.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear reporting of multiple seed runs, coherently derived from described methods, but raw simulation setups are not linked/open.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline. The results further demonstrate the efficiency of the ramp metering
nodes_sink.description: Contour plots showing speed distributions across time (8:00 to 9:00) and space (mainline distance) for No control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Results follow coherently from simulation but rely on unavailable SUMO configuration files and proprietary network calibration.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Line plots with shaded interquartile ranges comparing queue lengths at the on-ramp over time for the three scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Well-described metric aggregation; upstream reproducibility constrained by absent source code.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12 presents the mean queue lengths at the on-ramp and the red ratios (i.e., the proportion of the red phase in the simulation time) in each simulation for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Scatter plots with regression lines showing the relationship between mean queue lengths and red phase ratios for PI-ALINEA and Deep RL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Derived cleanly from 20 simulation outputs, but the simulation generator code itself is not shared.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 13 presents the queue lengths at the on-ramp and the occupancy downstream of the merging area for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Time series plots comparing occupancy (%) and queue length (m) side-by-side for PI-ALINEA and DRL over the simulation period.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear plot of two correlated metrics. Upstream generation requires reproducing the exact SUMO environment.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The better performance of the proposed DRL method is further revealed when considering traffic flows downstream of the merge area, which is demonstrated in Figure 14.
nodes_sink.description: Box plots comparing downstream traffic volumes across 5-minute intervals for No control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Summarizes simulation data effectively, though underlying raw vehicle trajectories and simulator configurations are not public.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed, and the baseline is the result of experiments that take original data as input.
nodes_sink.description: Box plot showing the distribution of travel times across 20 experiments for the baseline DRL and 8 perturbation scenarios where subarea information is masked.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: The perturbation method is clearly explained, allowing reconstruction if the base environment were provided.
